questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite hard, as I arrived with my partner, who is not studying. Student apartments provided through IDEALIS was only available for singles. Also, most student houses are only offering rooms for 1 person. We had to find accommodation through Short Stay Wageningen, which was quite expensive. However, if you register your address in Wageningen, you can apply for government housing support, which helps a lot with the rent - this is only if you have a self-contained studio (not only a room in a shared house).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is way nicer to live in town rather than at campus, as students tend to stay around in that area and not enjoy the cute town as much. However, I am not sure you can chose your accommodation yourself, since I did not go through IDEALIS. I would also go for houses, rather than the huge apartment buildings, that look like post-war buildings and are quite disgusting on the inside, as the students do not care about cleanliness (generally).

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was generally high, but some courses had a lower level than expected. If you study you can definitely pass your courses, but it is intensive to study here in general.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There is very little study material to read, which is sometimes a shame. Generally, all information is provided in lectures and you are expected to be present for lectures and practicals.
Lectures are short, only 45 min and you rarely experience 3-4 hour lectures as at UCPH. 
Every course includes groupwork and generally there is little individual work. I prefer less group work. 
You are often not allowed to use notes for exams, so most knowledge you need to know by heart, but also many exams are open questions, meaning you can write answers and do not have multiple choice.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Environmental Data Collection and Analysis because it introduces a broad range of different analysis to apply in R and because the fieldwork is fun and allows you to design your own experiment and analyze your own data.
Interdisciplinary Topics in Earth and Environment because you learn how to write a research proposal, make a review of a scientific article and also get a broad introduction to different interesting disciplinary topics. 
Biological Interactions in Soils because you set-up your own experiment regarding biology in soil and conduct lab work. 
Land degradation & development because it includes project work on a self-defined topic and explores differences in agriculture between e.g., conventional and organic agriculture. You conduct interviews with farmers and try to find out how land degradation can be adressed. 
Environmental Analytical Techniques because it is great to know all the techniques in the lab for the environmental analysis. 
The Soil Carbon dilemma because you learn to discuss carbon as a climate mitigation strategy and be critical to literature and public opinions

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go in spring! 
Prepare to study a lot and do lots of group work!
Arrive for the introduction week to ensure you meet people, if not you are quickly left out.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Academic learning

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making friends in autumn when I didn't arrive for the introduction week in early august.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The university relies on the two international student networks ESN and ISOW to arrange events for new students, however it is not working very well as most exchange students I meet do not like those associations or their events. I would have wished that the university had arranged events ONLY for exchange students, so that we could meet each other, as it is not the same to be on exchange as being an international student (ESN and ISOW are also open to international students and local students). I myself had to make a WhatsApp group and almost force the exchange team to share the link so that new students arriving in spring could join. This group allowed us to communicate before students even arrived.
